description: The Claude adapter's process rules: what ClaudeService does with each call, each stdout event and each exit, as the effects the platform carries out in order. publish assigns the adapter's published state (state, sessionID, modelName, totalCostUSD) at the points ClaudeService assigned it; resolveBinary and spawn launch the process, tagged with the launch generation; writeStdin writes one line (compared as JSON); closeStdin and terminateAfterGrace stop it; emit hands a harness event to the session. A line step is parsed, then fed event by event to the current generation, and its effects are the concatenation; retiredLine and retiredTerminated come from the previous generation. Request ids are the prefix "R", a dash and a count from 1.
function: ClaudeService's process rules ↔ powerup_core::harness::claude::adapter::ClaudeAdapter (request id prefix "R") — input {steps: [step]}; expected {effects: [[adapter effect]] (one list per step), snapshot: {state, sessionID, modelName, totalCostUSD} after the last step}
verifiedBy: Rust: rust/powerup-core/tests/harness.rs claude_adapter_cases runs ClaudeAdapter. ClaudeService still runs these rules in the app; the Swift suite plays this file once ClaudeService executes the core's effects (slice 2.3, #152).
capturedAgainst: Written from ClaudeService.swift of PowerUp at ae3de75 (start, finishStart, send, sendControlRequest, stop, apply and the termination handler), built with Swift 5.9.2 (Xcode 15.2); the Swift app cannot run these steps without a real process until #152

cases.name: a send before the spawn is queued and flushed on spawn
cases.reason: The binary is resolved off the main thread; a turn sent meanwhile is queued, marks the turn working, and is written the moment the process is up, never dropped (HK-079).

cases.name: a resumed start owns its session id at once
cases.reason: The hook echo guard and the protocol snapshot see the resumed id while the CLI is still starting; the id is published as given and only the argv trims it (HK-075).

cases.name: an override path is handed to the resolver
cases.reason: The platform resolves the binary (tilde, login shell, install spots); the core only passes the Settings path on.

cases.name: a missing binary stops with an error

event.message: claude CLI not found — set the path in Settings
Can't send that — the Claude session isn't running.

cases.reason: A launch that cannot find claude says so in words docs/troubleshooting.md quotes, drops the queued turn and the session id, and later sends are refused rather than queued.

cases.name: a failed spawn stops with an error

event.message: Couldn't start the claude CLI at /usr/local/bin/claude: The file is not executable.

cases.reason: Process.run() throwing ends the launch with the path and the reason; the queued requests go with it.

cases.name: a stop during resolution abandons the spawn
cases.reason: Stopping before the process exists marks it stopped, so the resolved binary is never spawned and the queued turn is dropped. A stop does not clear the session id; only an exit does.

cases.name: init gives sessionReady
cases.reason: system/init carries the live session id and model; the first one makes the session ready (HK-055, HK-073).

cases.name: an init after a send stays working
cases.reason: The CLI queues stdin while it boots, so a turn sent before init is already in flight; init must not downgrade it to ready (HK-073).

cases.name: a later init refreshes the model and keeps a working turn
cases.reason: The CLI re-emits init after a live set_model; every init refreshes the model (an empty one keeps it) and a repeated init never ends a working turn (HK-073).

cases.name: a later init after a stop reports ready again
cases.reason: A repeated init lifts a stopped or starting session to ready, even while the stopped process is still shutting down; ClaudeService always did, and the port keeps it (HK-073).

cases.name: a repeated assistant message is suppressed
cases.reason: The CLI repeats the assistant message once per content block, so an identical message right after itself is dropped; only the last one is remembered (HK-074).

cases.name: the de-dupe resets on turn end, send and init
cases.reason: A new turn may legitimately say the same thing again, so the memory is forgotten at each turn end, send and init (HK-074).

cases.name: costs accumulate across turns
cases.reason: The cost chip shows the session's total: each turn's total_cost_usd is added when it is finite and above zero, and zero, negative or missing costs never move it (HK-066). The test fake replaces the total instead, so only this table pins the sum.

cases.name: an error turn returns to ready
cases.reason: Every result ends the turn, an error one included, so the pad never stays busy (HK-064).

cases.name: text deltas and tool use pass through
cases.reason: Deltas and tool use change no adapter state; they reach the session in the order the line gave them (HK-060).

cases.name: a set_model ack refreshes the model at once
cases.reason: Waiting for the next init would leave the model chip a turn behind; the ack reports the trimmed value the request asked for (HK-071, HK-070).

cases.name: a failed set_model ack keeps the model
cases.reason: Only a successful ack changes the model; the failure reaches the session with its detail so it can roll the setting back (HK-071, HK-072).

cases.name: a permission mode ack reports its value
cases.reason: The ack names the subtype and the value recorded when the request went out, not the raw request id (HK-070).

cases.name: the interrupt ack has no value
cases.reason: An interrupt asks for no value, so its ack carries none (HK-070).

cases.name: an ack for an unknown or answered request is dropped
cases.reason: Only a request this launch made and has not seen answered is reported; anything else (a stale process, a request the CLI invented) is dropped (HK-070).

cases.name: request ids count the requests made
cases.reason: An empty model or mode sends nothing and takes no id (HK-068). Ids are the adapter's prefix and a count from 1; any unique string works (DESIGN.md v1.1 A, HK-396).

cases.name: control requests while starting are queued and recorded
cases.reason: A request made while the binary resolves is queued with the turns, in order, and its ack is still recognised (HK-068, HK-079).

cases.name: a control request without a session is dropped silently
cases.reason: Unlike a turn, a control request with no running process is dropped without an error: there is nothing to interrupt or switch.

cases.name: a send with no process is refused

event.message: Can't send that — the Claude session isn't running.

cases.reason: A turn is never silently dropped: with no session it is refused with a message (HK-079).

cases.name: a send to a dead process is refused

event.message: Can't send that — the Claude session isn't running.

cases.reason: The platform reports whether the process still runs; a dead one cannot take a turn (HK-079).

cases.name: an empty send writes nothing
cases.reason: A turn that trims to nothing is not sent and changes no state (HK-069).

cases.name: stop closes stdin, then a 2 s grace

event.message: Can't send that — the Claude session isn't running.

cases.reason: Closing stdin lets the CLI finish cleanly; the process is force-terminated only if it still runs after 2 s (HK-078). Stdin is closed once, so a second stop only arms another grace, and a send in between is refused.

cases.name: stop without a process
cases.reason: Nothing runs and nothing changes, so nothing is published.

cases.name: an unclean exit reports stderr
cases.reason: The CLI's last stderr words are the best explanation; the dead process no longer owns its session id (HK-076), while the model and the cost stay for the chip.

cases.name: an unclean exit without stderr says so
cases.reason: A kill or crash with nothing on stderr still explains itself with the code (HK-076).

cases.name: a clean exit is not an error
cases.reason: A clean exit reports no error even when stderr has text; the session id is cleared so the hook echo guard does not stay armed (HK-076).

cases.name: start while running stops first
cases.reason: A restart (effort change, resume retry) stops the running process first and starts a new launch generation; the cost total belongs to the app run and is kept.

cases.name: a new start drops the old in-flight requests
cases.reason: A reply from a retired process must not be attributed to the new one, so every start forgets the requests in flight (HK-070).

cases.name: a send between a restart and the old exit is refused

event.message: Can't send that — the Claude session isn't running.

cases.reason: Until the old process exits it is still the adapter's process, with its stdin closed, so a turn sent then is refused rather than queued; once it has exited, turns queue for the new launch again. ClaudeService behaved this way, and the port keeps it.

cases.name: a retired exit is ignored
cases.reason: The exit of a process a newer launch replaced must not stop the new session or report its stderr.

cases.name: lines of a retired generation are dropped
cases.reason: Output a replaced process flushes on its way out must not clobber the new launch's state.

cases.name: a write failure is reported

event.message: Couldn't reach the claude process: Broken pipe

cases.reason: A failed stdin write means the turn never reached the CLI; the session hears why.
